newsitem.title: CHINA: SHANGHAI SOYBEAN ENDS DOWN, OUTLOOK POOR.
newsitem.headline: SHANGHAI SOYBEAN ENDS DOWN, OUTLOOK POOR.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended down across the board on Thursday on short-selling by retail investors as technical charts showed a poor outlook.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,140 yuan ($378) per tonne, losing 20 yuan. It opened at 3,150 and hit a high of 3,155.
November fell one yuan to 3,141, the January 1998 contract 14 to 3,096 and March four to 3,100.
Combined volume rose to 20,800 tonnes from 16,600.
Soybeans opened mixed and fell for most of the session, traders said.
"Some retail investors are seen building short positions at high levels as technical charts showed a pessimistic outlook," one trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to fall further on Friday.
